Rechecking candidate divisor counts via prime factorization:

- \(120 = 2^3 \cdot 3 \cdot 5\), so \(\tau(120) = (3+1)(1+1)(1+1) = 16\).
- \(126 = 2 \cdot 3^2 \cdot 7\), so \(\tau(126) = (1+1)(2+1)(1+1) = 12\).
- Other high candidates below 150 have at most 15 divisors (e.g., \(144 = 2^4 \cdot 3^2\), \(\tau = 15\)).

Thus the maximum divisor count is 16, at column 120.

\boxed{120}
